description:
Hot-route capacity protection is a reliability program initiative at Redwood Inference to prevent fleet-wide impact when a small number of high-traffic or high-cost request routes (primarily top enterprise endpoints) surge or misbehave. The project adds tier-aware admission control across the request path—quotas/rate limits, priority routing (enterprise vs. self-serve), and graceful degradation behaviors—to ensure that overload events shed or defer lower-priority traffic while maintaining contractual SLOs for enterprise routes.

Goals:
- Protect the platform from cascading failures caused by sudden bursts, retries, or runaway clients on popular routes.
- Maintain latency and availability SLOs for top enterprise routes during partial capacity loss (GPU fleet degradation, regional issues, kernel regressions).
- Provide predictable, explainable behavior to customers (clear 429/over-capacity semantics, Retry-After guidance, and documented limits).
- Improve operational visibility: per-route/per-tier saturation signals, throttling dashboards, and alerting tied to error budgets.

Scope (in):
- API gateway enforcement for rate limits + quotas (per-tenant, per-route, per-region) with consistent response semantics.
- Smart Routing / policy engine changes to support priority lanes and capacity reservation for enterprise traffic.
- Data plane and runtime integration points for backpressure signals (queue depth, GPU utilization, prefill/decode saturation) used to trigger shedding.
- SRE-run rollout plan: feature flags, canaries, synthetic load tests, alert tuning, and incident playbooks.
- Customer support guidance and comms templates for throttling-related escalations.

Scope (out / non-goals):
- Major pricing/packaging redesign (only minor documentation alignment).
- Full per-customer dedicated scheduling inside kernels (handled separately by runtime scheduling roadmap).

Stakeholders:
- Engineering: Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park), Smart Routing (Mina Haddad), API Gateway (Amara Diallo), Quotas & Billing Hooks (Cole Summers), Data Plane (Vikram Singh), Runtime Scheduling (Sofia Ivanova) for backpressure signals.
- Reliability: SRE (Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes) for SLOs, monitoring, and incident process updates.
- Product: Hosted API (Nikhil Sharma) + Dedicated (Lauren Bishop) for customer-facing semantics and enterprise expectations.
- Support/CS: escalation handling and customer messaging for 429/over-capacity events.

Timeline (hypothetical):
- Phase 0 (Week 1–2): incident learnings + requirements (top routes list, tier definitions, initial SLO targets).
- Phase 1 (Week 3–5): design + ADRs (priority routing model, quota semantics, failure modes).
- Phase 2 (Week 6–9): implementation across gateway/policy/routing + observability.
- Phase 3 (Week 10–12): load testing, canary rollout, guardrail tuning, runbooks, and launch notes.

Key deliverables:
- Confluence design docs + ADRs + runbooks.
- Linear project plan with scoped engineering work.
- GitHub PRs implementing tier-aware throttling, routing, and dashboards.
- Slack coordination and incident simulations (game day) threads.
- A small number of support artifacts (Jira) and customer-facing alignment via sales/CS calls (Fireflies) and emails (Gmail).

files.description: Program brief: why hot-route protection is needed, target routes, reliability goals, success metrics, and ownership across SRE/Platform/Runtime.
PRD covering customer-facing behavior (429 semantics, Retry-After), tier definitions, rollout plan, and constraints for Hosted vs Dedicated.
Design spec for priority lanes in routing: policy evaluation, capacity reservation strategy, fairness model, and failure-mode behavior.
ADR documenting the chosen priority routing approach (e.g., strict priority with bounded starvation vs weighted fair queueing), rationale, and trade-offs.
ADR defining quota windows, burst handling, per-route keys, and standardized error response payloads for throttling.
Observability standard for metrics: per-route latency, throttled requests, saturation indicators, and recommended labels/cardinality constraints.
Service/system overview: how policy config is stored, evaluated, cached, and propagated to gateways/routers; includes diagrams and SLIs.
Dashboard spec: panels for throttling rate, queue depth, token/sec, GPU utilization, enterprise lane health; alert thresholds and links.
Proposed SLOs for top enterprise routes (availability + p95/p99 latency) with error budget policy and paging recommendations.
On-call runbook: diagnosing overload vs bug, verifying lane behavior, toggling protection flags, and customer comms checklist.
Game day plan: load generation steps, expected system behavior, rollback criteria, and post-exercise follow-ups.
Working doc with weekly updates, open questions, risk log, and decision backlog; links to Linear issues and relevant PRs.
Draft of config schema for per-route limits and priority rules; includes examples and migration notes (less polished than Confluence).
Spreadsheet-style doc: demand forecast for top routes, headroom assumptions, incident scenarios, and required reserved capacity buffers.
Notes from observability review focusing on metric labels, aggregation strategy, and performance/cost implications.
Draft customer-facing messaging and documentation snippets describing throttling behavior, guidance, and recommended client retries.
Linear project/umbrella issue: Hot-route capacity protection rollout plan, milestones, and tracking for cross-team work.
Implement per-route rate limiting in API gateway keyed by tenant + route + region; define config plumbing and default limits.
Add quota enforcement (daily/monthly) integration between telemetry metering and gateway enforcement; handle delayed metering and fail-open policy.
Priority lanes in router: enterprise lane admission + separate queueing; protect against starvation of lower tiers with bounded fairness.
Backpressure signal ingestion from runtime (queue depth, prefill saturation) into routing decisions; define thresholds and sampling.
Standardize throttling response payloads and headers (Retry-After, request id, policy reason codes) across gateway and router.
Add observability: metrics for throttled_count by route/tier, lane utilization, and per-route saturation indicators; ensure cardinality safety.
Canary + feature-flag framework for capacity protection policies; safe rollback and config validation.
Load test plan + perf-canary scenarios simulating bursty top-route traffic and retry storms; acceptance criteria tied to SLOs.
PM ticket: define enterprise throttling UX requirements, docs needs, and alignment with Dedicated commitments and SLAs.
PM ticket: pick initial ‘top enterprise routes’ list and rollout segmentation; includes stakeholder review and customer impact assessment.

PR: Add hot-route burst and retry-storm scenarios; gates merges on p95/p99 and error budget regression checks.
PR: Add per-route/per-tier SLO definitions and burn-rate alerts; supports enterprise lane-specific SLO reporting.
PR: Feature flag + rollout controls for hot-route protection; includes config kill-switch and staged rollout by region.
PR: Incident bot posts lane health summary and throttling spikes into incident channels; includes runbook links.
